clue.text: Key to fire engine?

parts.note: surface reading: the key that opens or works a fire engine, the red truck that fights fires
setter's reading: the key you turn to fire up, that is start, any car engine

explanation.walkthrough: The 'fire engine' picture hides the verb 'fire' meaning to start up a motor; the car key turns the system that sparks the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the starting system of a car, worked by turning a key so the engine fires into life.

clue.text: Grass with the blackened ends, so affected by 6?

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, as is to sing

indicators.note: ends are final letters, so only the last letter of each of these two words is kept

parts.note: the last letters of 'the' and 'blackened'

explanation.surface: Lawn grass scorched at its tips by something hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is LAVA, so the definition asks what something touched by molten lava would be: burnt at the surface. 'Grass' is the slang verb, not the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scorched lightly by molten rock is burnt at its surface, which is the past participle for a light burn.

clue.text: One leaving riotous Dáil Eireann in something of a rush?

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown out of order
something leaving departs, so that letter is taken out of the following name

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Irish parliament's lower house, taken letter for letter with the accent dropped

explanation.surface: A deputy storms out of a rowdy session of the Irish parliament in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dáil Eireann is the lower house of Ireland's parliament. One of its two I's goes, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released under stress is what people mean by a 'rush', so it is something of a rush.

clue.text: Atomic fire-starter in Zoroastrian writings?

parts.note: A is short for atomic, as in A-bomb
a vesta is a short wax match

explanation.surface: A nuclear arsonist turning up in ancient Persian scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is an old-fashioned word for a match, named after the Roman goddess of the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred texts of Zoroastrianism, the ancient Persian religion, are collected under this name.

clue.text: Glide over snow jolly hard, joining Iceland battle

parts.note: to ski is to glide over snow
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
IS is the international code for Iceland
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cheerful skier joins a fight in Iceland, the puzzle's theme country.
explanation.walkthrough: A jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, so it gives RM; 'jolly hard' is not 'very hard' here.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor fight between small forces is a kind of battle, smaller than a full engagement.

clue.text: Material discharged in 7 in flow around Valhalla's room?

indicators.note: flowing letters move freely and settle in a new order
only the letters lying around the inner part are kept, so the middle chunk is dropped

parts.note: the hall of the slain in Norse myth
a hall is a large room, and Valhalla's own room sits in its middle

explanation.surface: Molten matter streaming around the great hall of Norse legend.
explanation.walkthrough: VALHALLA is VAL + HALL + A, so what surrounds its room is VAL and A; those four letters are then rearranged. 7 is ERUPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Molten rock poured out of a volcano during an eruption is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: Event near 9 contaminated housing one occupies in turn?

indicators.note: turning round means reading the word back to front
a word housing something takes it inside like a building

parts.note: something contaminated is not pure
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something polluted near an Icelandic town, with residents taking turns to occupy a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contaminated' gives the two-word phrase NOT PURE, which reads backwards as ERUPTON before one goes in. 9 is GRINDAVIK, an Icelandic town near recent volcanic activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic outbursts near the Icelandic town of Grindavik in 2023 and 2024 were the news event behind the theme.

clue.text: Moon goddess observed start of 7 crossing lake

indicators.note: the word goes across the other, so it straddles it and holds it inside

parts.note: observed means seen
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: 7-down's answer begins with this letter

explanation.surface: The moon goddess watched an eruption begin across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of ERUPTION, the answer at 7, is added after SEEN has taken in L.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the moon was personified as this goddess, sister of Helios the sun.

clue.text: Polish king storing a rocket in town 7s threaten

indicators.note: a word storing something keeps it inside, as a cupboard does

parts.note: to grind is to polish a surface smooth
taken as written
the V-1 was the German flying bomb of the Second World War
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Polish monarch hoarding a missile inside a threatened town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb. The V-1 rocket is written VI.
explanation.definitionFit: This fishing town in south-west Iceland was evacuated as volcanic eruptions repeatedly threatened it.

clue.text: Where the eagle really landed: a backward country?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: backward means the name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Plays on 'The Eagle has landed', then jokes about an undeveloped country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Eagle has landed' was the Apollo 11 message; the clue says where a real eagle lands. 'backward country' looks like an insult but reverses EIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag is where the bird actually comes down to rest, and that nest has this name.

clue.text: One putting out second fire in room

indicators.note: putting something out removes it, so that letter is ejected

parts.note: a single is one
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone extinguishing a second blaze indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' and 'fire' both suggest firefighting, but 'putting out' removes a letter and the fire is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire burning on a domestic hearth, as in the inglenook beside it.

clue.text: Fruit from tree, poplar, best all but ruined

indicators.note: a ruined thing is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
all but means every letter except the final one is kept

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Fruit from a poplar, the best of it nearly all spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tree, poplar' looks like the definition pair, but the poplar is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree's small pear-like fruit goes by this hyphenated name, so it is a fruit produced by a tree.

clue.text: At home with divine huntress in state

parts.note: being in means being at home
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: The goddess of the hunt at home somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest, capital Indianapolis.

clue.text: 150 in 19? That's gentle on Fagradalsfjall

definitions.note: describes a slope rather than naming one; the answer is the noun

indicators.note: in places the first number inside the second

parts.note: the digits 1 and 9 read as I (Roman one) and NINE
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Reads like a cross-reference to 19, then remarks on a gentle Icelandic volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' is not a cross-reference to the clue at 19 across but the digits 1 and 9 spelt out separately. Fagradalsfjall is an Icelandic volcano whose slopes are fairly gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope that is not steep is a gentle rise, which is how the setter describes the volcano's flank.

clue.text: Entire crew needed, or staff in total one short?

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the second
one short means a single letter is missing from the end

parts.note: total in the sense of complete
staff are the workers, or men

explanation.surface: A manager complains that the whole crew is needed but the team is one person down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'total' loses its final E before the staff go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's full company of officers and sailors is called its complement, so the word means the whole crew.

clue.text: Single chap from east cut by Oscar's woman

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across entry means reading right to left

parts.note: I looks like the numeral one

indicators.note: a word cut by another is split and has it lodged inside

parts.note: a chap is a man
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: An unmarried man from the east is interrupted by Oscar's girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar's' looks possessive, but the apostrophe-s is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's given name, as of the biblical mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Working with beauty who might view 7 from 9?

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a looker is a good-looking person

explanation.surface: A working beauty watching the eruption from Grindavik.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is ERUPTION and 9 is GRINDAVIK, so the definition is someone watching the volcano from the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator who watches an event without taking part is the kind of person who would watch an eruption from a nearby town.

clue.text: When hot, what 22A may throw out in 7

parts.note: as in the sense of when
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Describes what a volcano scatters when hot and erupting.
explanation.walkthrough: 22A is VOLCANO and 7 is ERUPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic ash is the fine powdered rock that a volcano blasts out when it erupts.

clue.text: Stories after Edda initially included poetic reversal

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk

indicators.note: a letter that is included goes inside another word

parts.note: past in the sense of after, as in half past

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Edda

explanation.surface: Tales that follow the Norse Edda, included in a verse turnaround.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Norse poetry, fitting the theme. ANA is a crossword-familiar word for gathered anecdotes.
explanation.definitionFit: This metrical foot, two short syllables then a long one, is the dactyl turned round, so it is a poetic reversal.

clue.text: Pheasant from Sandringham on a ledge

indicators.note: from means taken out of the following words, lying inside them

parts.note: runs across the end of Sandringham through 'on a' into the start of ledge

explanation.surface: A game bird perched on a ledge at Sandringham, the royal estate in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandringham is a royal country estate in Norfolk, famous for its shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The monal is a brilliantly coloured Himalayan pheasant, a game bird of the same family.

clue.text: Explosive one contained by fat old polymath

indicators.note: contained by means held inside the words that follow

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: something explosive is blown apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A fat old genius with an explosive temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' fits the volcano theme but only rearranges the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, painter, engineer and inventor, is the classic example of a polymath.

clue.text: Crater in collapsed 22A about to devour tree

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow, so one word ends up inside the other

parts.note: ca, from circa, means about
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A crater inside a fallen-in volcano is about to swallow a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 22A is VOLCANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is the large basin left when a volcano's summit collapses into its emptied magma chamber.

clue.text: Clubs do something with American plant

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to act is to do something
US for American

explanation.surface: Clubs taking action over an American plant, perhaps a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory in the surface; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny succulent, a type of plant from dry regions of the Americas.

clue.text: O look! See about saving ass! In Fagradalsfjall?

definitions.note: the answer is something found at Fagradalsfjall; the question mark flags the example

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe inside
about means turned round, so the three items are read in the opposite order

parts.note: taken as written
lo is an old word for look
V is short for vide, Latin for see
can is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone shouting in alarm at a donkey that needs rescuing on an Icelandic mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ass' is not the donkey but American slang for a bottom. Fagradalsfjall is a volcanic system in south-west Iceland that erupted in 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagradalsfjall is a mountain on Iceland's Reykjanes peninsula whose fissures are an active volcano.

clue.text: God of fire in delta-wing bomber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Roman god of fire and the forge
second meaning: the British triangle-winged V-bomber of the Cold War

explanation.surface: A fire god flying in a Cold War aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman smith-god gave his name to the Avro aircraft, a triangular-winged British nuclear bomber.

clue.text: Green mineral water taken by fool cycling?

indicators.note: the fool is taken in, so it ends up inside the other word
cycling moves the front letter round to the back, like a wheel turning

parts.note: eau is French for water
git is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A green mineral water drunk by a fool out cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The French water's first letter moves to its end, and the fool goes inside. Git is everyday British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Augite is a dark green to black pyroxene, a mineral common in volcanic rocks such as basalt.

clue.text: Complete justification for narrow escape

parts.note: to close a deal is to complete it
call as in 'no call for that', a reason or justification

explanation.surface: A full excuse offered for a lucky getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where disaster was only just avoided is a near miss, the same as a narrow escape.

clue.text: Just for finishers, time is up by clock

indicators.note: finishers are the final letters, and only those count

parts.note: the final letters of time, is and up
the final letter of by

explanation.surface: A race official calling time on the finishers, with the clock running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is the slang verb meaning to notice, not the timepiece the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock someone, in informal British use, is to notice or catch sight of them, which is to espy.

clue.text: Molten rock in periodical almost duplicated?

indicators.note: repeated but not quite in full, so the copy lacks its last letter

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: Molten rock featured in a magazine that has nearly been printed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The magazine word is written once in full and then again without its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is the term for molten rock while it is still underground, before it erupts as lava.

clue.text: Run through advice for deployment of parasol?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: exhaust or consume completely
second meaning: instructions for a sunshade, read as two commands: put it to work, then raise it

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading of the phrase as an imperative pair, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To run through money or supplies is to exhaust them entirely; the phrasal verb means the same.

clue.text: Spooner's badger set forth — became still

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to badger is to nag and to set forth is to have stated; Spooner swaps the opening sounds of that pair

explanation.surface: An animal home set out, and then everything went quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger set' looks like the animal's burrow (a sett), but the words split into two separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or an economy that stopped moving or developing is said to have stagnated, so it became still.
